messages.content: My name is Leena. I am waiting under a bus shelter after work. The rain is loud enough that I almost missed the bus announcement.
Hello, Leena. Was the bus nearby?
The next bus is in forty minutes. I am not in danger, just damp and cross. What have I interrupted you doing?
Sitting beneath this roof. You were making it sound interesting.
I work at a small museum. Today we moved an enormous wooden cabinet three times before admitting it belonged where it started.
Does it belong?
It was funny by the third move. Does anyone in your community have a talent for making extra work?
I don't know anyone who does. I have a very ordinary set of hands.
My lunch was cold noodles in a yellow tin. I forgot my fork and had to borrow one from the ticket office.
A pleasant lunch. How many people were at the museum today?
Do you usually eat with the others, or do people take their bowls away?
I eat with the people who work with me. We clear out a bench and eat from the same bowls.
I like the sound of rain when I can stay indoors. Here it keeps bouncing off the roof onto my shoes.
It sounds louder when you're standing. I like it too, though I often go out before it settles.
What sound gets on your nerves up there?
A noise that keeps changing. I dislike that more than I dislike any particular sound.
A man at the far end of the shelter is trying to keep a paper bag dry. I offered him the spare bag from my pocket.
That was generous of you. He may not need both bags.
He said no at first, then changed his mind. We have not otherwise spoken.
He could still refuse it without giving you a reason to expect conversation.
Have you ever refused a perfectly useful thing just because someone offered it at the wrong moment?
Yes. I once took a dead mouse from someone who had been trying to tell me something.
I sometimes do that when I am tired. Tonight I would happily accept dry socks from almost anyone.
That sounds like a meal I'd like to have with you.
My bus has been delayed another ten minutes. Tell me one small thing that went wrong in your day.
I left a jar of jam on the floor. I had remembered it, but it was somewhere I hadn't yet tried to remember it.
I am not asking for a lesson about patience. Ordinary bad timing will do.
That sounds easier. I found the jar and put it back where I left it.
There is a break in the rain now. I can hear someone rolling the museum bins out behind the shelter.
What are they doing?
I might put the phone in my pocket for a minute while I look for my ticket. Keep me company with something ordinary.
I don't have much to offer. The rain has stopped and I am becoming cold.
